name: Shemaiah
overview: Shemaiah is a male member of the tribe of Levi, noted specifically as the son of Harim who had married a foreign wife. This detail highlights his unique attribute within the post-exilic community, emphasizing the challenges faced regarding intermarriage. No additional notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Shemaiah means 'YHWH hears,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's attentiveness. This proper name, as recorded in Ezra 10:21, does not indicate it was given directly by God but carries a meaningful connection to divine hearing.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Shemaiah as a descendant of Harim, establishing his family lineage within the tribe of Levi. Beyond this, no further family relationships are documented in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Shemaiah's significance lies in his identification as a Levite who was part of the group grappling with the issue of foreign marriages after the exile. His mention in Ezra 10:21 situates him within the broader narrative of Israel's covenantal faithfulness and restoration, underscoring the community's efforts to maintain purity according to God's commands.
